transcript: Chapter 35. Kiva. One door each. Kellan was at the draft board at eight, in the black and gold, reading his own card with his hands in his pockets. Kiva saw him from across the boards and went over. She had meant to find him at the loft and had missed him. He had gone down the stair at six, Prue said, before anybody else was dressed, with his boots in his hand, so as not to wake the room. Now he stood alone in front of the deal board, with the green bays along its top, and there were nineteen cards on it, and he was reading the one with the Halden mark at its head, as though it were a sum that would not come out.
